facts.text: Rinard was named after Adam Rinard, a business partner of Bonham, who helped establish the community in the late 19th century.
The town’s first railroad depot, built in 1870, was the second structure erected in Rinard, marking the start of its rail‑era growth.
Surveyed in 1870, Rinard grew around a side track that shipped trainloads of oats, making it a key agricultural hub for the region.
George Leach’s Brick and Tile Factory, another early industry, supplied building materials to surrounding towns during Rinard’s formative years.
Jacob’s Chapel, founded by settler Jacob Feathers, began as a simple log structure and remains a historic reminder of Rinard’s pioneer roots.
